layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For some years now, many workers have been active in the development

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a stainless steel that is resistant to pitting and crevice corrosion in halide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: media. Electrochemical techniques combined with statistical multiple-regres-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion analysis have beeen used to derive a relationship between pitting sus-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ceptibility and chemical composition. Recent publications in the literature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have suggested, however, that the use of electrochemical accelerated tests

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for pitting corrosion studies leads to erroneous conclusions about the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: susceptibility of alloys. This paper describes the results of a program de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: signed to investigate the above reports and firmly establish whether indeed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrochemical techniques can be used as valid accelerated tests in pitting-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion studies.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Extensive experimental investigation in 1M sodium chloride on Type 430

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steel have shown an excellent correlation between electrochemical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and chemical techniques, both in visually observed pitting susceptibility and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal weight loss data. Further, data obtained in 1M sodium chloride con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taining different dissolved gases have indicated why other authors failed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting tests, Values of the critical breakdown potential were found to vary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Evidence has been presented which demonstrates the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complete correspondence between the pitting corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavior of Type 430 stainless steel in accelerated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrochemical and chemical tests. On the basis of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polarization measurements and controlled potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion studies, discrepancies previously reported

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between the two test methods can be satisfactorily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explained.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The specific relation of the critical breakdown po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tential to pit initiation and not to pit propagation has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been demonstrated, along with confirmation of the pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: viously reported fact that pit propagation may proceed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at potentials active to the breakdown potential.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It has been shown that extreme caution must be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used when utilizing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as an index of pitting corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: susceptibility, since the absolute magnitude of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been demonstrated to vary not only with the well-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: documented environmental and experimental variables,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but also with the nature of the gases dissolved in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrodent.
